newsitem.title: INDIA: India rupee ends higher though RBI buys dollars.
newsitem.headline: India rupee ends higher though RBI buys dollars.

text.p: The Indian rupee closed higher against the dollar at 35.70/71 on Tuesday despite last-minute intervention by the central bank, dealers said.
The rupee opened the day steady at 35.72/73, the level to which RBI had dragged it through its end-of-the-day dollar purchases on Monday.
The RBI intervened 10 minutes before the market closed, buying dollars at 35.71 in contrast to Monday's purchases upto the 35.73 level, dealers said.
Near the close of trade, dealers vowed to test on Wednesday the Reserve Bank of India's (RBI) intention to hold down the rupee.

"For two days in succession, he intervened at the end of the day," said the chief dealer at a Bombay bank, referring to the RBI. "The market will test him much earlier tomorrow to force a decision," he said.
The rupee had been expected to rise as it had on Monday, but the movement was delayed as the State Bank of India (SBI) bid for the U.S. currency in the morning session at 35.725/735.
This proved to be a one-off demand which soon petered out.
SBI soon started selling dollars, triggering the dollar's fall, dealers said.
"It was the market versus the RBI," a dealer said.

The market kept teasing the central bank, with screen quotes fluctuating between 35.70/71. The RBI made enquiries but did not buy until the quotes pierced the 35.70-mark with deals at 35.695, dealers said.
"The market will test his intentions earlier tomorrow," a dealer added.
